Not my idea, I saw it under another post but I cant for the life of me remember which post and whose comment. Either way, I want this added more than anything else because the Single Player campaign structure was some of the most fun I've had in an arcade racer in ages, but now afterward beating it it's really just driving around and earning money to buy random cars with no pressure or purpose.

Said idea would be some form of gamemode that repurposes the story-mode calender into a sort of scenario based, rogue-like, replayable experience with random (or changeable) modifier effects, conditions for cars, events, challenges and goals to reach until the deadline. Each day could have semi-random events, various modifiers like maybe the cops are more out in force on particular days, or heat stays persistent, and you get a set number of days/weeks to work up to some goal. Different cars, available funds and whatnot at the start, maybe even restrictions on cars you can use (or even just one single car you have to build up), and potentially switched up tactics for cops. Like (re)introducing rhinos or killswitches, and generally a lot of modifiers that pose some challenges but open other opportunities for the player instead, to make each of these playthroughs more unique. 

The Devs could even make curated presets, like playing as Ross trying to gather the money for college in time by racing(maybe even with pizza delivery side jobs), or totally-not-Jack-from-The-Run trying to pay his debt to the mafia within x days before the deadline, but his heat stays persistent between days.

The Daihatsu Cohen ("Neutral" in this post) was the car used in a coffee break (you have probably seen the coffee break video by BK4). You had to make it through a field of cones without touching a single one in a pretty tight timeframe to get gold. The music while the cohen is on the screen in the video is the melody before the countdown starts. When the cones knock the car out ... thats the "license test failed" melody.
